item.text: I’m treating this as a chapter dossier build for 4B, reusing only prior evidence that genuinely fits political-freedom lenses and then filling the remaining gaps with targeted primary and independent sources.

item.text:
**Reused Evidence**
- `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0024"],"lenses":["4B.3","4B.6"]}`
- `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0030"],"lenses":["4B.6","4B.9"]}`

**New Evidence**
- AMLO's April 2022 electoral-reform pitch is the clearest ruler-authored statement pushing on electoral rules.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"28.04.22 Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador","publisher":"Presidencia de México","publication_date":"2022-04-28","url":"https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/28-04-22-version-estenografica-de-la-conferencia-de-prensa-matutina-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador/","claim":"AMLO said his administration would send a constitutional electoral-reform proposal to Congress to guarantee clean and free elections and to leave behind electoral fraud.","locator":"lines 31-33","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct presidential transcript, but the claim is the ruler's own framing of a politically contested reform.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 conduct and justification for changing electoral rules.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO as the initiator of the reform package.","contrary_evidence":["Critics argued the reform would weaken electoral independence rather than protect it.","The source is self-justifying and does not prove the reform would actually improve democracy."],"lenses":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.10"]}`

- In November 2022, AMLO explicitly denied that the reform was a reelection vehicle.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"16.11.22 Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador","publisher":"Presidencia de México","publication_date":"2022-11-16","url":"https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/16-11-22-version-estenografica-de-la-conferencia-de-prensa-matutina-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador/","claim":"AMLO said the accusation that the reform sought his reelection was false and that the reform did not propose presidential reelection.","locator":"lines 327-330","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct ruler statement in an official transcript, but embedded in a partisan information campaign.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 statement about transfer rules and succession.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's own public position.","contrary_evidence":["The same transcript also promotes a broad electoral overhaul that critics said would weaken independent institutions.","Self-denial is not independent proof of future compliance."],"lenses":["4B.1","4B.8"]}`

- The 2022 recall process is a strong contestability data point, even though it was non-binding and low-turnout.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Realiza INE declaratoria de resultados del proceso de Revocación de Mandato","publisher":"Instituto Nacional Electoral (Central Electoral)","publication_date":"2022-04-11","url":"https://centralelectoral.ine.mx/2022/04/11/realiza-ine-declaratoria-de-resultados-del-proceso-de-revocacion-de-mandato/","claim":"INE completed the 2022 recall count, reporting 17.77% participation and 91.86% for López Obrador to stay in office; the INE leadership described the day as a free, secret, peaceful civic exercise.","locator":"lines 147-160","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Contemporaneous official election administrator record with exact vote totals and procedural description.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 ruler-period evidence of contestability and transfer rules.","ruler_attribution":"AMLO was the sitting president subjected to the legally organized recall process; the source shows the institution ran and counted the vote, not that he created the rules.","contrary_evidence":["The result was non-binding because participation fell well short of the 40% legal threshold.","A recall is not the same as a full competitive general election."],"lenses":["4B.1","4B.8","4B.10"]}`

- Congress blocked the reform, which is important counterevidence to full capture but also shows the executive tried to change the system.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexican Congress rejects president's electoral reform bid","publisher":"Reuters","publication_date":"2022-12-06","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexican-congress-rejects-presidents-electoral-reform-bid-2958679","claim":"Mexico's lower house rejected AMLO's controversial electoral reform after critics said it could undermine the country's electoral independence.","locator":"lead paragraph","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters reporting on a contemporaneous legislative defeat and the stated criticism of the proposal.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 evidence of conflict over electoral independence.","ruler_attribution":"The reform was backed by López Obrador, but the institutional rejection came from Congress, not from him alone.","contrary_evidence":["The bill failed in Congress, so the executive did not fully capture the electoral rules in 2022.","Reuters frames the concern as critics' assessment, not a judicial finding."],"lenses":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.10"]}`

- Mexico's state elections in 2022 still produced opposition wins, so the system remained electorally contestable.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexican president's party wins most states in Sunday elections","publisher":"Reuters (via MarketScreener)","publication_date":"2022-06-06","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Mexican-president-s-party-wins-most-states-in-Sunday-elections--40647270/","claim":"MORENA and its allies won four of six state elections, while opposition candidates led in Aguascalientes and Durango; all six states had started the day in opposition hands.","locator":"lead paragraph","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters election reporting with preliminary official counts and clear competitive results.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 election evidence during AMLO's presidency.","ruler_attribution":"The elections occurred under AMLO's administration, but the source does not show him directing the count or suppressing the opposition.","contrary_evidence":["This is subnational evidence, not a national presidential contest.","MORENA's gains also show the president's party remained electorally strong."],"lenses":["4B.1","4B.3","4B.10"]}`

- Reuters Institute describes a sustained hostile posture toward critical media.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexico | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","publisher":"Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","publication_date":"2022-06-15","url":"https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2022/mexico","claim":"AMLO's daily morning briefings had become hostile to parts of the media; in July 2021 he added a 'Who's Who' segment that singles out journalists and publications, and the report says he classifies media into 'good' and 'bad'.","locator":"lines 33-35","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Oxford-based research summary describing the president's public communication pattern and media treatment.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly relevant to 2022 information environment and ruler conduct in office.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's own communications style and public briefings.","contrary_evidence":["The report is descriptive rather than legal; it does not by itself establish formal censorship or state orders.","Mexico still had plural media outlets and criticism remained public."],"lenses":["4B.3","4B.6"]}`

- ARTICLE 19's annual review gives the strongest aggregate press-freedom baseline for 2022.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexico: Voices Against Indifference","publisher":"ARTICLE 19","publication_date":"2023-03-28","url":"https://www.article19.org/resources/mexico-voices-against-indifference/","claim":"ARTICLE 19 reported 696 attacks against the press in Mexico in 2022, 12 journalists murdered, 42.53% of documented attacks perpetrated directly by state actors, and 176 stigmatizing executive comments against the media, journalists, and civil-society organizations.","locator":"lines 69-77","source_type":"ngo","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Annual monitoring report with explicit 2022 counts and attribution categories.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Retrospective but directly about 2022 conduct and environment.","ruler_attribution":"The report ties the pattern to the current administration's public discourse and media ecosystem, but not every attack is personally ordered by AMLO.","contrary_evidence":["The report is about documented attacks, not every unreported incident.","Some attacks were subnational or non-federal, so presidential attribution is partial."],"lenses":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.10"]}`

- The Pegasus evidence is strong for illicit surveillance, but attribution to AMLO personally remains incomplete.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"New Pegasus Spyware Abuses Identified in Mexico","publisher":"The Citizen Lab","publication_date":"2022-10-02","url":"https://citizenlab.ca/research/new-pegasus-spyware-abuses-identified-in-mexico/","claim":"R3D and Citizen Lab found that Mexican journalists and a human rights defender were infected with Pegasus between 2019 and 2021, after Mexico's president had assured the public the government no longer used the spyware and that there would be no further abuses.","locator":"lines 62 and 126-132","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Technical forensic validation by a university lab, with explicit limits on attribution to a particular customer.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Target-period relevant because the infections span into the AMLO years and were publicly reported in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The source places the infections during AMLO's government and after his public assurance, but does not identify the specific customer or direct order giver.","contrary_evidence":["The lab explicitly says it could not attribute the hacking to a particular NSO customer.","The infections span 2019-2021, so the source is only partly target-year specific."],"lenses":["4B.6","4B.9"]}`

- The UN human-rights office described the surveillance as arbitrary interference with an intimidating effect.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"La ONU-DH expresa su preocupación por actos de vigilancia ilícita contra personas defensoras de derechos humanos y periodistas","publisher":"Naciones Unidas en México","publication_date":"2022-10-11","url":"https://mexico.un.org/es/202890-la-onu-dh-expresa-su-preocupaci%C3%B3n-por-actos-de-vigilancia-il%C3%ADcita-contra-personas-defensoras","claim":"The UN human-rights office said illicit surveillance against journalists and human-rights defenders constituted arbitrary interference, came to light through leaked Sedena documents or a government-acquired software package, and had an intimidating effect that signaled intolerance of criticism.","locator":"lines 59-66","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official UN human-rights statement issued contemporaneously in Mexico with direct normative assessment.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 evidence about the ruler-period information environment and state surveillance concerns.","ruler_attribution":"The statement concerns state institutions under the AMLO government, but does not directly name the top-level order giver.","contrary_evidence":["The UN note stops short of naming AMLO personally as the person who ordered surveillance.","It is a human-rights concern statement, not a court finding."],"lenses":["4B.6","4B.9"]}`

- The biometric-registry ruling is useful context for court independence and a government-backed privacy overreach.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexico's top court strikes down controversial cellphone registry with biometric data","publisher":"Reuters via Euronews","publication_date":"2022-04-25","url":"https://www.euronews.com/next/2022/04/25/mexico-telecoms","claim":"Mexico's Supreme Court ruled that a national cellphone-user registry with biometric data was unconstitutional, dealing a blow to López Obrador's government, which had backed the measure.","locator":"lead paragraph","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters reporting on a direct court ruling against a government-backed surveillance proposal.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Direct 2022 evidence of institutional constraint and a government-backed surveillance proposal.","ruler_attribution":"The measure was backed by AMLO's government, but the constraint was imposed by the Supreme Court rather than by AMLO himself.","contrary_evidence":["The ruling is judicial constraint, not proof that AMLO strengthened courts.","The source does not show the final fate of other privacy or surveillance proposals in 2022."],"lenses":["4B.4","4B.9"]}`

**Search and Rejection Summary**
- I considered roughly 30 documents across presidential transcripts, INE materials, Reuters/Reuters Institute reporting, ARTICLE 19, Citizen Lab, UN human-rights output, and Reuters court coverage.
- I retained 10 distinct URLs because they added non-duplicative 2022 evidence on contestable elections, term-limit/reelection claims, electoral reform, media pressure, surveillance, and institutional constraint.
- I rejected duplicate Reuters image/licensing pages, broad background explainers that added no ruler-specific 2022 fact, and later follow-ups from 2023-2026 when a 2022 source already covered the point.
- I also dropped out-of-period material unless it clearly functioned as a retrospective summary of 2022 conduct, as in the ARTICLE 19 annual report.
- I did not reuse generic democracy baselines as direct ruler evidence unless they tied to a concrete 2022 choice, speech, reform, or constraint.

**Remaining Gaps**
- Direct proof that López Obrador personally ordered surveillance or media harassment is still incomplete; the evidence is strong on public rhetoric and state-linked abuse, weaker on command chain.
- The 2022 record on appointments to autonomous bodies like INE, INAI, and the CNDH would sharpen 4B.4 and 4B.5 further.
- I did not find a clean 2022 source on internet shutdowns or formal censorship; the dossier rests on stigmatization, budget/resource pressure, electoral-rule reform, and surveillance.
- More search would help if you want tighter attribution on whether subordinate institutions acted under explicit presidential direction versus tolerated drift.
